title.narrative: Urban SHADE (Strengthening Health Access and Delivery for Extreme weather)

description.narrative: 1. To retrospectively assess the health and social vulnerabilities and health service impacts of specific recent extreme weather events (including floods, storms and extreme heat) and among urban marginalized people. 2. To assess the preparedness and capacities of health systems for delivering health services during and after extreme weather events, drawing on existing frameworks, policies and institutional mechanisms. 3. To co-produce and implement with communities, health systems and governance actors a package of research informed interventions to strengthen health service preparedness and delivery during and following extreme weather events. 4.To strengthen the capacities and collaborative processes of researchers, community groups, health system and governance actors to work equitable in improving responsiveness to climate related challenges. 5. To collaboratively monitor and evaluate the feasibility, fidelity, cost and contextual enablers or barriers of implementing the co-designed interventions within and across diverse urban settings. 6. To promote dissemination and uptake of project learning by communities, health system actors, policymakers and researchers to inform climate resilient health systems and policies.

The Urban SHADE (Strengthening Health Access and Delivery for Extreme Weather Events) project is a multi-country and multi-institutional initiative led by Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine and implemented by The George Institute for Global Health in India, in collaboration with partners in Kenya and Sierra Leone. The project aims to strengthen the resilience and responsiveness of health service delivery during Extreme Weather Events (EWEs) among urban marginalized communities in India. In the context of climate change urban poor living in informal settlements face compounded health risks such as heat stress, vector-borne diseases, respiratory illnesses and injuries alongside other major disruptions to health service delivery.
This research study seeks to build climate-resilient and equitable health systems through Participatory Action Research (PAR) that actively involves communities, governance actors, and health system stakeholders in identifying vulnerabilities, co-producing interventions and fostering institutional responses. By applying a mixed method approach, this study aims to enhance preparedness, responsiveness and adaptive capacity of urban health systems to withstand and recover from extreme weather events. In India, this study is conducted in across 5 settlements in three cities - Shimla in Himachal Pradesh and Guntur and Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh. This project will generate evidence on the vulnerabilities of urban marginalised populations, gaps in the health service delivery, and opportunities for co-designed interventions that can strengthen policy and programmatic action for climate and health resilience. The research emphasises equitable partnerships, capacity strengthening and policy uptake to promote sustainable health outcomes for vulnerable urban populations.
